I saved a revision checklist on your bus essay covering all nine comments. It runs from 9:00 to 11:40 tonight, with time for you to submit before the 11:59 p.m. deadline. Dr. Weiss allows AI help with planning, so the essay revisions are yours to make.

Start with the one-year trial on routes 14 and 22 that you propose in your conclusion. Bring that proposal into the opening, then use your roommate’s forty-minute walk to show why the fare matters. To build your 391-word draft toward the roughly 1,000-word target, spend most of your time on two questions: How much did ridership change in Riverton, according to which source? How would the city cover lost fares during the trial? The checklist leaves the comma fixes for the final pass.

detail.text: 9:00–9:15 p.m. Read paragraph 5 beside paragraph 1. Put your proposal for a one-year fare-free trial on the 14 and 22 near the start. Which detail from your daily ride or your roommate’s walk best explains why you want the council to try it? In the conclusion, return to what the council should learn from counting riders.
